causal:influence:aadc_activity:negative:.evidence: Brun L et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2010 (AADC deficiency: elevated urinary vanillactic acid as diagnostic biomarker); Hyland K & Clayton PT, J Neurochem 1992 (vanillactic acid elevated in AADC-deficient patients: the L-DOPA->3-OMD->vanillactate shunt pathway); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (AADC/DDC deficiency, OMIM 608643: elevated L-DOPA and vanillactic acid metabolites) | intervention: AADC deficiency (DDC gene LoF, OMIM 608643): do(aadc_activity=low) -> L-DOPA accumulates -> urinary_vanillactate rises
causal:influence:aadc_activity:negative:.mechanism: when AADC is deficient, L-DOPA cannot be decarboxylated to dopamine and instead accumulates; excess L-DOPA is O-methylated by COMT to 3-O-methylDOPA (3-OMD) and further catabolised via reductive metabolism to vanillactic acid (3-methoxy-4-hydroxyphenyllactic acid); thus AADC deficiency (lower enzyme activity) causes a shunt toward vanillactate, raising its urinary excretion; higher AADC activity consumes L-DOPA normally, reducing the shunt to vanillactate

causal:influence:adamts13_activity:negat.evidence: Inborn error: Upshaw-Schulman syndrome / congenital TTP (ADAMTS13 biallelic LoF mutations, OMIM 274150) — severe thrombocytopenia and microvascular platelet activation due to UL-VWF-driven platelet aggregation; Zheng et al. 2004 Blood 107:3161 (complete ADAMTS13 deficiency is prothrombotic); ASH Hematology Education 2012 (Role of ADAMTS13 in TTP pathogenesis). Williams Hematology (ADAMTS13 and VWF multimer size regulation). | intervention: ADAMTS13 biallelic loss-of-function (Upshaw-Schulman syndrome, OMIM 274150): do(adamts13_activity ↓) → UL-VWF accumulation → platelet_activation ↑, confirming sign '-'.

When ADAMTS13 activity is high, UL-VWF strings are rapidly trimmed, limiting spontaneous VWF-platelet binding and platelet activation. When ADAMTS13 activity is low, UL-VWF accumulates on endothelial surfaces and in plasma, recruiting and activating platelets to form microvascular platelet thrombi.

causal:influence:adsl_activity:negative:.evidence: ADSL deficiency OMIM 103050; Jaeken & Van den Berghe, Science 1984 (both SAdo and SAICAr elevated); Ciardo et al., Neurology 1992 (ADSL deficiency markers: SAdo and SAICAr in urine). | intervention: do(ADSL LoF, OMIM 103050) — SAICAr (the dephosphorylated SAICAR riboside) accumulates and is excreted in urine
causal:influence:adsl_activity:negative:.mechanism: ADSL also cleaves SAICAR (succinylaminoimidazolecarboxamide ribotide) to AICAR in de novo purine synthesis; ADSL deficiency causes SAICAR accumulation; the dephosphorylated riboside form (SAICAr) appears in urine alongside succinyladenosine.

causal:influence:aicda_deaminase_activit.evidence: HIGM2 (OMIM 605258): elevated serum IgM; hyper-IgM syndromes review (Update on hyper immunoglobulin M syndromes, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2010). | intervention: do(AICDA LoF) — no class-switch; B cells remain IgM-secreting; serum IgM elevated in HIGM2 [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:aldh7a1_activity:negati.evidence: Pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy / ALDH7A1 deficiency (OMIM 266100); ScienceDirect — 'Clinical, biochemical, molecular and therapeutic aspects of 2 new cases of 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase deficiency'; PMC1378037 — AASS gene identification with elevated alpha-AASA in familial hyperlysinemia; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (lysine catabolism pathway). | intervention: do(ALDH7A1 activity ↓) = pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy / ALDH7A1 deficiency (OMIM 266100)
causal:influence:aldh7a1_activity:negati.mechanism: Alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH7A1 / antiquitin) oxidises alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde (alpha-AASA) to alpha-aminoadipate; alpha-AASA is in rapid equilibrium with Δ1-piperideine-6-carboxylate. ALDH7A1 deficiency (pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy) → alpha-AASA cannot be cleared → plasma level rises (∂[AASA]/∂(ALDH7A1 activity) < 0).

causal:influence:alpha_aminoadipic_semia.mechanism: AASS (the bifunctional lysine-ketoglutarate reductase/saccharopine dehydrogenase) initiates lysine catabolism; reduced activity causes lysine to accumulate (hyperlysinemia)

causal:influence:alveolar_po2:positive:p.mechanism: low alveolar PO2 constricts arterioles in the hypoxic region, diverting/reducing local blood flow

causal:influence:aromatase_activity:posi.evidence: Bulun et al. PMC7952251 (Estrogen disorders: aromatase in granulosa cells); Simpson et al. (2002) TRENDS Endocrinol Metab 13:158-163 (aromatase biology); aromatase-excess syndrome (OMIM:139300) — gain-of-function CYP19A1 mutation causes elevated granulosa/adipose estradiol, gynecomastia and precocious feminization; aromatase deficiency (OMIM:107910) — LoF CYP19A1 causes absent estradiol production and virilization; Williams Textbook of Endocrinology (ovarian steroidogenesis: granulosa aromatase drives follicular estradiol output). | intervention: Aromatase deficiency (CYP19A1 LoF, OMIM:107910): granulosa-cell aromatase is absent -> estradiol secretion falls to essentially zero -> severe estrogen deficiency with virilization; aromatase inhibitor therapy (anastrozole, letrozole) similarly abolishes granulosa estradiol output; aromatase-excess syndrome (GoF) markedly raises estradiol.
causal:influence:aromatase_activity:posi.mechanism: Aromatase (CYP19A1) in ovarian granulosa cells catalyses the rate-limiting aromatization of androstenedione (supplied by theca cells) to estrone, and testosterone to 17β-estradiol; higher aromatase activity directly increases granulosa-cell estradiol secretion rate (two-cell two-gonadotropin model). FSH induces CYP19A1 transcription via cAMP/PKA in granulosa cells; granulosa-cell aromatase is the dominant source of circulating estradiol in pre-menopausal women.

causal:influence:arterial_po2:positive:m.evidence: Tissue hypoxia can be due to (1) a low P O2 in arterial blood caused, for example, by pulmonary disease (hypoxic hypoxia)
causal:influence:arterial_po2:positive:m.mechanism: a low arterial PO2 lowers capillary PO2 and hence tissue PO2 (hypoxic hypoxia)

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: MSUD (OMIM 248600); NBK557773 — 'elevated plasma alloisoleucine is pathognomonic for classic MSUD; formed by keto-enol tautomerisation and amination of the 2-oxoacid derivative of isoleucine'; myadlm.org MSUD review — alloisoleucine elevation is a distinguishing characteristic of MSUD. | intervention: do(BCKDH complex activity ↓) = maple syrup urine disease (OMIM 248600)

Elevated plasma alloisoleucine is pathognomonic for MSUD.

[citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:bmp6_ligand:positive:bm.evidence: Ganz & Nemeth 2012 (Biochim Biophys Acta 1823:1434-1443, PMID 22306005); BioModels BIOMD0000000734 (Parmar et al. 2017, BMC Syst Biol 11:57). [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:carbonic_anhydrase_ii_a.evidence: CA2 deficiency (OMIM 259730, autosomal recessive osteopetrosis with RTA): CA2-knockout mice show bicarbonaturia and alkaline urine consistent with type III RTA. Sly et al., NEJM 1983 / PMID 6405388. Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (proximal tubule bicarbonate reabsorption; role of CA2). | intervention: do(CA2 activity DOWN) — carbonic anhydrase II deficiency (OMIM 259730) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:carbonic_anhydrase_ii_a.mechanism: CA2 in proximal tubule cells catalyzes luminal CO2+H2O -> H2CO3 -> H+ + HCO3-; cytosolic CA2 also generates H+ for luminal NHE-3, driving bicarbonate reclamation. CA2 LoF impairs H+ secretion and bicarbonate reabsorption, causing proximal + distal bicarbonate wasting (bicarbonaturia). More CA2 activity = more bicarbonate reclaimed = less in urine.

causal:influence:catalase_activity:negat.evidence: PMC7016158 'Effect of hydrogen peroxide on normal and acatalasemic mouse erythrocytes' (acatalasaemia → elevated intracellular H2O2, increased methemoglobin); ScienceDirect 'Importance of Catalase in the Disposal of Hydrogen Peroxide Within Human Erythrocytes' (catalase handles ~50% of H2O2 generated in red cells); news-medical.net acatalasaemia review (CAT deficiency → H2O2 accumulation in erythrocytes). | intervention: loss-of-function of CAT (acatalasaemia) raises erythrocyte hydrogen peroxide
causal:influence:catalase_activity:negat.mechanism: Catalase catalyses the decomposition of H2O2 to H2O + O2 in erythrocytes; it is the principal defence against H2O2 in red cells (with glutathione peroxidase). Acatalasaemia (CAT LoF, OMIM #614097) causes H2O2 to accumulate in erythrocytes, leading to oxidative haemoglobin damage and methemoglobin formation.

causal:influence:cbs_enzyme_activity:neg.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 22 (transsulfuration: cystathionine beta-synthase, homocysteine + serine -> cystathionine); classic homocystinuria OMIM 236200
causal:influence:cbs_enzyme_activity:neg.mechanism: CBS condenses homocysteine with serine to cystathionine (first transsulfuration step); homocysteine is the SUBSTRATE, so ∂[Hcy]/∂(CBS activity) < 0 — LoF (activity DOWN) => homocysteine accumulates.

causal:influence:comt_activity:positive:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (catecholamine catabolism: COMT + MAO pathways; epinephrine -> metanephrine via COMT); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (catecholamine inactivation: O-methylation by COMT); Williams Textbook of Endocrinology (fractionated urinary metanephrines in pheochromocytoma diagnosis; metanephrine is the O-methylated epinephrine catabolite) | intervention: pharmacological: COMT inhibitors (entacapone/tolcapone): do(comt_activity=low) -> urinary_metanephrine falls; pheochromocytoma increases substrate (epinephrine) and COMT converts it, raising metanephrine
causal:influence:comt_activity:positive:.mechanism: catechol O-methyltransferase O-methylates epinephrine to metanephrine (and norepinephrine to normetanephrine) as the principal inactivation pathway; higher COMT activity converts more epinephrine to metanephrine, raising urinary metanephrine; COMT inhibitors (tolcapone, entacapone) pharmacologically reduce metanephrine production

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: "An increase in total circulating cholesterol and triglycerides is observed"; "Hepatic lipoprotein synthesis is stimulated, and increases in circulating cholesterol and triglycerides may be found" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p. 496, 502  ||  "Glucocorticoids have robust effects on multiple aspects of lipid metabolism, inducing expression of HMG-CoA reductase to promote cholesterol synthesis, increasing expression of fatty acid synthase to promote fatty acid synthesis, and decreasing LPL to impair clearance of circulating lipids. Accordingly, hyperlipidemia is commonly seen in the setting of glucocorticoid treatment." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 41, p. 1587
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: glucocorticoids increase lipolysis and stimulate hepatic lipoprotein synthesis → elevated circulating triglycerides

causal:influence:csf_sepiapterin:positiv.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthesis & salvage); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (sepiapterin-reductase deficiency: raised CSF sepiapterin and BH2, low BH4)
causal:influence:csf_sepiapterin:positiv.mechanism: sepiapterin is reduced by sepiapterin reductase / aldo-keto reductases to 7,8-dihydrobiopterin (BH2) in the salvage pathway; a larger sepiapterin pool feeds more BH2 (product formation)

causal:influence:cyp11b2_activity:positi.evidence: CYP11B2 aldosterone synthase deficiency (isolated hypoaldosteronism, OMIM 203400); Aldosterone synthase Wikipedia; PMC3976226 — clinical significance of CYP11B2 deficiency (salt-wasting, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, low aldosterone); PNAS 1992 — CYP11B2 mutations causing corticosterone methyloxidase II deficiency; PMC10118833 (congenital hyperreninemic hypoaldosteronism). CYP11B2 activity directly produces aldosterone in zona glomerulosa. | intervention: CYP11B2 LoF (aldosterone synthase deficiency): aldosterone secretion from zona glomerulosa falls -> salt wasting; angiotensin II / potassium stimulate CYP11B2 -> aldosterone secretion increases
causal:influence:cyp11b2_activity:positi.mechanism: CYP11B2 (aldosterone synthase) is expressed exclusively in adrenal zona glomerulosa and catalyses all three terminal steps of aldosterone biosynthesis: 11-beta-hydroxylation of DOC to corticosterone, 18-hydroxylation to 18-hydroxycorticosterone, and 18-methyl oxidation to aldosterone. CYP11B2 activity is the sole determinant of zona glomerulosa aldosterone output; LoF causes isolated aldosterone synthase deficiency with salt-wasting.

causal:influence:cyp17a1_activity:positi.evidence: CYP17A1 deficiency (congenital adrenal hyperplasia, 17-alpha-hydroxylase/lyase deficiency; OMIM 202110): loss of CYP17A1 lyase activity causes DHEA to fall; gain restores/elevates it. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, Ch. 15 (adrenal steroidogenesis: pregnenolone -> 17-OH-pregnenolone -> DHEA via CYP17A1 hydroxylase+lyase). | intervention: CYP17A1 loss-of-function (OMIM 202110): DHEA falls; gain of CYP17A1 lyase activity raises DHEA
causal:influence:cyp17a1_activity:positi.mechanism: CYP17A1 lyase activity cleaves the side chain of 17-hydroxypregnenolone to produce DHEA in adrenal zona reticularis; greater enzyme activity yields more DHEA product

causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:negati.evidence: 21-hydroxylase deficiency (congenital adrenal hyperplasia), OMIM:201910 — LoF causes massive 17-hydroxyprogesterone accumulation in plasma
causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:negati.mechanism: RHEA:50308 (EC 1.14.15.15): 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone + reduced [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + O2 = 11-deoxycortisol + oxidized [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + H2O + H(+); 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone is the substrate

causal:influence:cyp2a6_activity:positiv.evidence: Fernandez-Salguero et al. (Nicotine metabolite ratio as index of CYP2A6 activity). Benowitz et al. PMC3617060 (The ability of plasma cotinine to predict nicotine exposure is altered by CYP2A6 differences). | intervention: do(CYP2A6 LoF/GoF) — CYP2A6 activity level determines plasma cotinine from a fixed nicotine dose [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cyp2a6_activity:positiv.mechanism: CYP2A6 is responsible for ~90% of hepatic nicotine metabolism to cotinine via C-oxidation; CYP2A6 poor metabolizers (LoF variants) produce significantly less cotinine from a given nicotine dose, while extensive metabolizers show higher cotinine from the same nicotine exposure.

causal:influence:cyp7a1_activity:positiv.evidence: Bile acid synthesis defect type 1 OMIM 603540 (CYP7A1 LoF leads to reduced bile acid production and hypercholesterolemia); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Ch. 26 (CYP7A1 rate-limiting for bile acid synthesis); Schwarz et al., J Clin Invest 1998 (CYP7A1 deficiency in humans). | intervention: CYP7A1 loss-of-function (bile acid synthesis defect type 1, OMIM 603540): CYP7A1 LoF -> reduced bile acid synthesis -> reduced fecal bile acid excretion
causal:influence:cyp7a1_activity:positiv.mechanism: CYP7A1 (cholesterol 7alpha-monooxygenase) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the classical (neutral) bile-acid synthesis pathway. More CYP7A1 activity drives greater bile acid synthesis, increases the bile acid pool, and elevates fecal bile acid excretion. CYP7A1 deficiency reduces the bile acid pool and fecal bile acid output.

causal:influence:cystinosin_activity:pos.evidence: Nephropathic cystinosis (CTNS deficiency, OMIM 219800): Gahl et al. (2002) N Engl J Med 347:111-121 (cystinosis: lysosomal cystine accumulation -> Fanconi syndrome -> progressive renal failure, GFR decline); Town et al. (1998) Nat Genet 18:319-324 (CTNS cloning: cystinosin as lysosomal cystine transporter); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (cystinosis: renal Fanconi syndrome, end-stage renal disease). Intervention: do(CTNS LoF). | intervention: genetic loss-of-function of CTNS (nephropathic cystinosis, OMIM 219800)
causal:influence:cystinosin_activity:pos.mechanism: Cystinosin (CTNS) is the lysosomal cystine transporter that exports cystine from lysosomes to the cytoplasm for further metabolism. Cystinosin deficiency (nephropathic cystinosis, OMIM 219800) causes cystine to accumulate in lysosomes of renal proximal tubular cells, leading to proximal tubular dysfunction (Fanconi syndrome), progressive tubular and glomerular damage, and chronic kidney disease with declining GFR. Active cystinosin maintains lysosomal cystine homeostasis and preserves renal tubular and glomerular function, sustaining GFR.

causal:influence:cytosolic_calcium_trans.evidence: Bers (2001) Excitation-Contraction Coupling: cytosolic Ca2+ binds troponin C to activate the myofilaments; BioModels MODEL7914464799 (Shannon2004, PubMed 15347581) includes cTnC as the dominant cytosolic Ca2+ buffer / activation site. | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-107 (19.3: Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity): calcium ions combine with the regulatory protein troponin in the troponin-tropomyosin complex, removing inhibition of myosin cross-bridge formation with actin active sites to produce contraction; Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-12.9 (Cell Motility - Undeclared): 'When Ca2+ is available, it can bind to troponin-C, leading to a conformational change that shifts the position of tropomyosin to reveal the myosin binding site.'; Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-5.5.7 (Summary): 'Ca²⁺ binding to troponin-C triggers conformational changes that displace tropomyosin, thereby initiating contraction by allowing myosin heads to interact with actin.' [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cytosolic_calcium_trans.mechanism: rising cytosolic free Ca2+ binds the regulatory N-lobe of cardiac troponin C (quality: cytosolic [Ca2+] -> disposition: cTnC Ca2+ affinity -> process: Ca2+ binding to cTnC -> quality: fractional Ca2+ occupancy of cTnC / thin-filament activation)

causal:influence:dhcr24_activity:positiv.evidence: Waterham HR et al. Am J Hum Genet. 2001;69:685-694 (desmosterolosis; DHCR24 LoF causes desmosterol accumulation and cholesterol deficit); OMIM 602398 (desmosterolosis); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, cholesterol biosynthesis (Bloch pathway: desmosterol -> cholesterol via DHCR24). Intervention: DHCR24 loss-of-function (desmosterolosis, OMIM 602398): do(DHCR24 activity down) -> hepatic cholesterol synthesis impaired.
causal:influence:dhcr24_activity:positiv.mechanism: DHCR24 (Delta(24)-sterol reductase / 3-beta-hydroxysterol Delta24-reductase) reduces the C24=C25 double bond of desmosterol to produce cholesterol, the final step of the Bloch pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis. DHCR24 loss-of-function (desmosterolosis, OMIM 602398) blocks this terminal step, causing desmosterol to accumulate to high levels in plasma and tissues while hepatic cholesterol synthesis is severely impaired.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.evidence: Dihydropyrimidinase deficiency OMIM 222748; van Kuilenburg et al., Biochim Biophys Acta 2004 (DPYS deficiency: dihydrouracil and dihydrothymine elevated); Hamajima et al., Pediatr Int 2009. | intervention: do(DPYS LoF, OMIM 222748) — dihydrothymine accumulates, urinary excretion rises
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.mechanism: DPYS also ring-opens 5,6-dihydrothymine (thymine pathway analog of dihydrouracil) to N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate; DPYS deficiency causes dihydrothymine accumulation and urinary excretion.

causal:influence:duodenal_lipase_activit.evidence: Lowe ME 2002 J Lipid Res 43:2007-2016 — pancreatic lipase is the principal enzyme for dietary fat digestion; OMIM 614337 (pancreatic lipase deficiency): severe steatorrhea, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, low plasma FFA postprandially; Jakubowski & Flatt Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §lipid digestion: pancreatic lipase + colipase hydrolyse TG → FFA + 2-MAG → absorbed → chylomicron → plasma FFA. | intervention: do(duodenal_lipase_activity -) — orlistat (gastric/pancreatic lipase inhibitor) blocks fat digestion, reducing plasma postprandial FFA; do(duodenal_lipase_activity +) — exogenous pancrelipase (pancreatic enzyme replacement) restores fat absorption and plasma FFA in exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
causal:influence:duodenal_lipase_activit.mechanism: Pancreatic lipase (PNLIP) hydrolyses dietary triglycerides at the sn-1 and sn-3 positions in the duodenal lumen, releasing 2-monoacylglycerol and free fatty acids. These are incorporated into mixed micelles and absorbed across the enterocyte brush border; FFA are re-esterified into triglycerides, assembled into chylomicrons, and secreted into lymph and then blood, raising plasma FFA. Congenital pancreatic lipase deficiency (OMIM 614337) causes severe fat malabsorption and reduced postprandial plasma FFA, confirming the causal link.

causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.evidence: ECHS1 deficiency, OMIM:616277 — LoF is associated with elevated urinary 3-hydroxyisobutyric acid, a valine catabolism marker
causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.mechanism: RHEA:31175 (EC 4.2.1.17): 2-methylpropenoyl-CoA (methacrylyl-CoA) + H2O = (S)-3-hydroxyisobutanoyl-CoA; physiological direction: methacrylyl-CoA is the valine-pathway substrate of ECHS1; (S)-3-hydroxyisobutanoyl-CoA -> 3-hydroxyisobutyrate (CHEBI:18064); LoF accumulates methacrylyl-CoA upstream and shunts to urinary 3-hydroxyisobutyrate via alternative routes

causal:influence:endothelial_no_producti.evidence: "administration of drugs that inhibit this normal formation of nitric oxide increases renal vascular resistance and decreases GFR and urinary sodium excretion" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 26 (Urine Formation I), p 322
causal:influence:endothelial_no_producti.mechanism: endothelial NO -> vascular smooth-muscle cGMP -> renal arteriolar relaxation -> lowered renal vascular resistance; NOS inhibitors raise RVR and lower GFR/Na excretion

causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyruvate_ki.evidence: PKLR deficiency OMIM 266200; Frontiers Pediatrics PMC9752143 (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal jaundice in severe PKLR deficiency); Harrison's 'Haemolytic Anaemia' (indirect bilirubin rises due to haem catabolism); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 23 (haem degradation pathway). | intervention: do(erythrocyte_pyruvate_kinase_activity ↓) — PKLR deficiency OMIM 266200
causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyruvate_ki.mechanism: Haemolysis from PKLR deficiency releases haem from destroyed erythrocytes; haem is catabolised via haem oxygenase → biliverdin → unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin, which accumulates in plasma when haemolysis exceeds hepatic conjugation capacity, causing jaundice.

causal:influence:etfdh_activity:negative.evidence: Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; OMIM 231680 (MADD / glutaric aciduria type II): urinary organic-acid profile includes short-chain 3-hydroxy fatty acids; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 17 (short-chain beta-oxidation intermediates) | intervention: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (ETFDH loss-of-function, OMIM 231680)
causal:influence:etfdh_activity:negative.mechanism: ETFDH deficiency (MADD) impairs short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenation including that of 3-hydroxypentanoyl-CoA intermediates; reduced ETFDH activity leads to accumulation of 3-hydroxypentanoic acid excreted in urine
